answer: Each identity anchors to one registered terraced paddy plot on karst hills, leased at $120 a year plus a $35 water sensor. Every epoch the plot must report fresh flow readings from its shale-lined channels, checked against the irrigation district registry: one plot, one vote. Shared readings collapse to a single identity and forged flows burn a $50 stake. A farm wanting 1,000 votes must lease 1,000 real plots and keep 1,000 real water flows running, about $155,000 a year, with cost rising linearly per fake; an honest farmer pays once and reuses the same plot.
